findings.note: lateCapDoerRaised is a package-level mutable bool shared across the test binary. Benign here (single test writes it, no t.Parallel in this file), but it is global test state that would silently break if a parallel test were ever added or the test were run twice in one process via -count.

findings.note: isOutputCapBody's generic markers ('output limit was reached' / 'output limit reached') are substring matches on the lowercased whole body; a future gateway that phrases a content-filter or quota refusal with the literal phrase 'output limit reached' would be misrouted into one doomed 4x retry before failing terminally. Cost is one wasted request, not a wrong verdict; the marker set is pinned by TestIsOutputCapBody and is documented as deliberately tight.

findings.note: withBody's cap read is a comma-ok type assertion on int. If a future prepare() path writes the cap as a non-int (int64/float), capKey silently stays "" and a cap 400 becomes terminal with no retry and no error signal. Guarded today by construction (both provider paths write int) and by the terminal-fail-not-corrupt branch at judge.go:696-704, but it is an implicit invariant rather than a checked one.
